ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fixation Overlay Benchmark for Egocentric Intent Questions
PROPOSAL: Assemble 800 short first-person clips from a public egocentric dataset with recorded eye tracking, and write a multiple-choice question for each about what the wearer attends to or will do next. Draw the recorded fixation as a coloured ring on eight evenly spaced frames and query four open multimodal models with the same instruction. Score accuracy per question type with bootstrap intervals over clips.
CONTROLS: Run the same models on the same frames without the ring, on frames carrying a ring from a different clip, and with the ring at the image centre. Add a text-only run that sees the question and options alone. Repeat over three seeds of option order.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Rings at the true fixation should improve accuracy on attention questions more than on next-action questions. The result fails to support the idea if accuracy with the true ring is within bootstrap error of the ring-free run.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fixation Crops as Extra Visual Tokens
PROPOSAL: Extend an open seven-billion-parameter multimodal model so that each sampled frame is accompanied by a high-detail crop centred on the recorded fixation, encoded by the same vision tower and appended to the visual token sequence after a learned separator embedding. Fine-tune only the projection layer and a low-rank adapter on 15000 gaze-linked questions drawn from public egocentric recordings, then test on held-out wearers. Measure accuracy on questions about attention and about the next action.
CONTROLS: Compare against the unmodified model on the same held-out questions, against a model given the same crop taken at a displaced point, and against a model fine-tuned on identical questions with only global frames. Repeat the runs over three seeds.
COST: 1400
PREDICTION: Crops should help most when the attended object is small in the global frame. The extension fails if the displaced-crop model scores close to the true-crop model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adapting a Multimodal Model to Read Gaze Cues
PROPOSAL: Synthesise 20000 question-answer pairs from egocentric recordings with eye tracking, where each answer names the object under the fixation or the action that follows it, and fine-tune a seven-billion-parameter open multimodal model on them with low-rank adapters. Optimise the adapter rank and learning rate on a validation split of unseen wearers, then test on wearers and kitchens absent from training. Analyse behaviour separately on questions that need the gaze trace and on questions answerable from scene content alone.
CONTROLS: Compare with the original model, with an adapter trained on the same questions after removing the gaze marker, and with an adapter trained on markers taken from the wrong clips. Hold the test questions fixed and repeat over three seeds.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: The adapted model should gain mainly on gaze-dependent questions and little on scene-only questions. A comparable gain on both kinds would suggest it learned the question style rather than the gaze cue.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gaze Noise Tolerance of Fixation Cues
PROPOSAL: Take 600 egocentric questions with recorded eye tracking and perturb the fixation point by Gaussian offsets of 0, 1, 2, 4 and 8 degrees of visual angle before drawing it on each frame. Query three open multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and record accuracy per offset. Add a second perturbation that mimics a consumer head-mounted tracker, using a calibration drift that grows over the course of each clip. Plot accuracy against offset for each question type.
CONTROLS: Compare each offset against the undisturbed fixation, against frames without a cue, and against a cue at a location from another moment of the same clip. Repeat over three seeds of the perturbation.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Accuracy should fall towards the cue-free level around the offset where the marker leaves the attended object. The idea fails if accuracy stays flat across all offsets, since that would show the models ignore the marker.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparing Four Ways to Show Gaze to a Multimodal Model
PROPOSAL: Present the recorded fixation four ways: a ring on the frame, a heat map blended over the frame, a high-detail crop appended as a second image, and the pixel coordinates written into the prompt. Use 1000 intent questions over egocentric clips from public eye-tracking datasets, and test three open-weight models of different sizes with a fixed instruction per format. Compute accuracy per format and per question type, with bootstrap intervals over clips.
CONTROLS: Include a run with no gaze cue, a run with each format built from a fixation taken from another clip, and a text-only run. Repeat over three seeds of option order.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: The crop and ring formats should lead on small-object questions, while coordinates in text should help least because models rarely see such numbers tied to pixels. The comparison is uninformative if all four formats land within bootstrap error of the cue-free run.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gaze History Window for Predicting Wearer Intent
PROPOSAL: Vary the temporal window of fixation history shown to a multimodal model, from the current frame alone to the previous two seconds, by drawing fading rings for each past fixation on a single frame. Use 900 next-action questions over egocentric clips with eye tracking, query two open models with a fixed instruction, and measure accuracy for each window length. Break results down by whether the next action involves the most recently fixated object.
CONTROLS: Compare each window against a frame without rings and against windows built from another clip. Add a text-only run and repeat over three seeds of option order.
COST: 260
PREDICTION: Accuracy should rise for short windows and flatten once the window reaches about one second. The idea fails if the longest window scores below the single-fixation condition.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Annotator Agreement on Gaze-Dependent Intent Questions
PROPOSAL: We run a validation study of 300 candidate intent questions on egocentric clips with eye tracking. Twelve annotators answer each question twice, once watching the clip and once watching it with the fixation trace drawn on the frames, and we keep the questions where the trace changes the majority answer. We then give the retained questions to three open multimodal models with and without the trace and compare their accuracy with that of the annotators.
CONTROLS: We compare annotators who see the trace of the correct clip with annotators who see the trace of another clip, and we add a group that answers from the question text alone. We measure agreement with Krippendorff's alpha and repeat the model runs over three seeds of option order.
COST: 12
PREDICTION: We expect the trace to change the majority answer for roughly a third of questions about attention and for few next-action questions. We count the study as failed if text-only annotators reach the accuracy of annotators who see the trace.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dwell-Time Triggers for Proactive Assistant Suggestions
PROPOSAL: Simulate a proactive assistant on 500 egocentric clips with eye tracking, where a suggestion appears whenever the fixation rests on one object longer than a threshold. Generate each suggestion with an open multimodal model given the frames and the fixated object, then have raters score relevance and timeliness on a five-point scale. Vary the threshold across 200, 400, 800 and 1600 milliseconds.
CONTROLS: Compare against suggestions triggered at random moments, at scene changes, and at fixed intervals, using the same generator and the same raters. Repeat over three seeds of the random trigger.
COST: 35
PREDICTION: Dwell-triggered suggestions should earn higher relevance ratings than random ones, with the best threshold near 400 milliseconds. The idea fails if raters cannot tell dwell-triggered suggestions from random-trigger suggestions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Failure Analysis of Gaze-Free Intent Answers
PROPOSAL: Run four open multimodal models without any gaze cue on 700 intent questions over egocentric clips, and sort every wrong answer into categories: wrong object, right object but wrong action, wrong time, or ambiguous question. Have two annotators label a random half of the errors and report their agreement. Count how many errors involve objects that the wearer never fixated.
CONTROLS: Run the same sorting on answers from a text-only model, and on answers given with the fixation drawn on frames, to see which categories the cue removes. Repeat the model runs over three seeds of option order.
COST: 24
PREDICTION: Most gaze-free errors should be wrong-object errors on items far from the fixation. The analysis fails to support the idea if the cue leaves the category counts unchanged.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fixation-Guided Frame Selection for Egocentric Questions
PROPOSAL: Choose eight frames per clip at moments when the fixation lands on a new object, rather than sampling them uniformly, and feed them to two open multimodal models alongside the question. Use 1000 intent questions on egocentric clips with recorded eye tracking. Measure accuracy per question type and the share of answer-relevant objects visible in the chosen frames.
CONTROLS: Compare with uniform sampling, with sampling at scene changes, and with fixation-selected frames from another clip, keeping the frame count fixed. Repeat over three seeds of option order.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Fixation-selected frames should help on next-action questions where the key object appears briefly. The idea fails if uniform sampling covers as many answer-relevant objects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fixation Rings Versus Plain Frames on Intent Questions
PROPOSAL: Build 1200 multiple-choice questions on short first-person clips from Ego4D and EGTEA Gaze+, asking what the wearer will do next or which object holds attention. Draw each recorded fixation as a red ring on eight sampled frames, then query Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3-8B with one prompt that names the ring. Score answer accuracy by question type, with bootstrap intervals across clips.
CONTROLS: Compare the ring condition against the same eight frames shown without a ring, using the same prompts. Compare against a ring drawn at a fixation taken from a different clip. Compare against a ring placed at the frame centre. Repeat over 3 seeds of option order.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: The ring should raise accuracy on attention questions more than on forecast questions. The claim fails if ring and plain frames score within bootstrap error of each other.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Frame Sampling Density and Fixation Rings on Intent Questions
PROPOSAL: Assemble 1200 multiple-choice questions over brief egocentric recordings from Ego-Exo4D and Aria Everyday Activities, about the wearer's next step or the object under attention. Draw every measured fixation as a red ring on sixteen sampled frames, and put the questions to LLaVA-OneVision-7B and Qwen2.5-VL-7B with a prompt that names the ring. Tabulate answer accuracy per question type, with bootstrap intervals across clips.
CONTROLS: Compare the ring condition against the same sixteen frames re-encoded at lower quality, using the same prompts. Compare against a ring drawn in a different colour. Compare against the larger variant of the model without a ring. Repeat over 3 seeds of option order.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: The ring should raise accuracy on attention questions above forecast questions. The claim fails if ring and quality-reduced frames score within bootstrap error of each other.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gaze Noise Tolerance of Fixation-Marked Frames
PROPOSAL: Take 900 intent questions on egocentric clips with tracked fixations and mark the fixation on each sampled frame. Displace the marked point by a Gaussian offset with standard deviation of 0, 1, 2, 4 and 8 degrees of visual angle, then ask Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3-8B to answer. Plot accuracy against displacement for each question type and read off where the benefit of the mark disappears.
CONTROLS: Compare each displaced condition against the undisturbed fixation, using the same prompts. Compare against a point drawn at a location from another moment of the same clip. Compare against frames without a mark drawn. Repeat over 3 seeds of the displacement.
COST: 560
PREDICTION: Accuracy should decay towards the unmarked level as the offset grows. The claim fails if accuracy drops to the unmarked level already at the smallest offset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Frame Count Tolerance of Fixation-Marked Frames
PROPOSAL: Draw the measured gaze point on every frame sampled for 900 intent questions about tracked egocentric clips. Reduce the number of sampled frames to 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 per clip, then ask Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3-8B to answer. Plot accuracy against frame count for each question type and read off where the benefit of extra frames disappears.
CONTROLS: Compare each frame count against the 32-frame input, using the same prompts. Compare against frames sampled at a different rate from the same clip. Compare against frames re-encoded at lower quality. Repeat over 3 seeds of the sampling offset.
COST: 560
PREDICTION: Accuracy should climb with frame count and then flatten. The claim fails if accuracy with the fewest frames already reaches the level of the fullest input.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Teaching a Multimodal Model to Read Fixation Marks
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune Qwen2.5-VL-7B with low-rank adapters on 20000 synthetic questions built from egocentric clips, each tied to the object under the recorded fixation, with answers composed from object and narration labels. Evaluate on clips and kitchens absent from training, using hand-written questions about attention and next action. Report accuracy for gaze-dependent items and for items answerable from the scene alone.
CONTROLS: Compare the adapted model against the original model on the same held-out items. Compare against a model adapted on the same questions with the marks moved to another clip. Compare held-out kitchens against training kitchens. Repeat over 3 seeds of adapter initialization.
COST: 2100
PREDICTION: Gains should concentrate on gaze-dependent items. The claim fails if the adapted model improves to the same degree on scene-only items.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gaze-Mark Adapters Evaluated on Third-Person Cooking Videos
PROPOSAL: Adapt InternVL3-8B with low-rank adapters on 20000 synthetic questions built from egocentric clips, each tied to the object under the recorded fixation, with answers composed from object and narration labels. Evaluate on third-person recordings of cooking and on a general video question benchmark, using hand-written questions about objects and actions. Report accuracy for marked items and for items without marks.
CONTROLS: Compare the adapted model against the original model on the same third-person items. Compare against a model adapted on the same questions with the answer order permuted. Compare third-person clips against training clips. Repeat over 3 seeds of adapter initialization.
COST: 2100
PREDICTION: Gains should concentrate on marked items. The claim fails if the adapted model improves to the same degree on unmarked items.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Intent Reading Without Gaze Across Open Multimodal Models
PROPOSAL: Collect 600 egocentric clips, each with a person-written question about the wearer's goal and four answer options, validated by two annotators. Run six open multimodal models in zero-shot mode on the frames alone, with a single instruction wording, and mark each chosen option as matching the annotators' label or not. Break results down by question type and by clip length.
CONTROLS: Compare each model against the annotators on the same questions. Compare against a text-only run that sees the question and options alone. Compare against a run with option order permuted. Repeat over 3 seeds of frame sampling.
COST: 70
PREDICTION: Accuracy should rise with model scale yet stay far from annotator level on intent questions. The claim fails if the text-only run scores close to the video runs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Answer Confidence of Open Multimodal Models on Egocentric Questions
PROPOSAL: Gather 600 first-person recordings, each with a hand-written question on the wearer's next wish and four answer options, validated by two annotators. Prompt six open multimodal models zero-shot on the frames alone, with a single instruction wording, and store the probability of the chosen option together with the length and fluency of a free-text rationale. Group the stored values by question type and by clip length.
CONTROLS: Compare each model against a language-model scorer on the same rationales. Compare against a text-only run that sees the question and options alone. Compare against a run with option order permuted. Repeat over 3 seeds of frame sampling.
COST: 70
PREDICTION: Confidence should rise with model scale yet stay far from annotator-rated fluency on intent questions. The claim fails if the text-only run scores close to the video runs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Four Ways to Present Fixation to a Multimodal Model
PROPOSAL: Present the recorded fixation as a ring on the frame, as a heat map blended into the frame, as a high-detail crop appended as a second image, and as pixel coordinates in the prompt. Use 1000 intent questions on egocentric clips with eye tracking and test Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3-8B with one fixed instruction per format. Compute accuracy per format and per question type, with bootstrap intervals across clips.
CONTROLS: Compare each format against the others on the same questions and frames. Compare against frames shown without any fixation cue. Compare against each format built from a fixation taken from another clip. Repeat over 3 seeds of option order.
COST: 520
PREDICTION: The ring and crop formats should lead on small-object questions, with pixel coordinates trailing. The claim fails if all four formats land within bootstrap error of the cue-free run.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Frame Layouts for Fixation-Marked Egocentric Questions
PROPOSAL: Show the ring-marked fixation with sixteen frames tiled in a grid, with sixteen frames as a sequence of separate images, with eight frames upscaled, and with eight frames at the original size. Use 1000 intent questions on egocentric clips with eye tracking and test Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3-8B with one fixed instruction per layout. Compute accuracy per layout and per question type, with bootstrap intervals across clips.
CONTROLS: Compare each layout against the others on the same questions and frames. Compare against frames shown at a doubled frame count. Compare against each layout built from the fixation after temporal smoothing. Repeat over 3 seeds of option order.
COST: 520
PREDICTION: The grid and sequence layouts should lead on small-object questions, with upscaled frames trailing. The claim fails if all four layouts land within bootstrap error of the original-size run.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gaze-Dependent Intent Questions for Egocentric Video
PROPOSAL: Write questions whose correct answer changes with the fixation, by pairing each clip with two fixation segments that point at different objects and two matching answers. Check each item with annotators who see the clip with the gaze trace and annotators who see it without, and keep items where the two groups choose different answers. Evaluate open multimodal models on the retained set with and without the gaze trace drawn on frames.
CONTROLS: Check agreement between annotators on retained items. Check that retained items cannot be answered by a text-only run. Check the per-object balance of answers. Report accuracy per question type.
COST: 850
PREDICTION: Models should score near chance on retained items without the gaze trace, and above chance with it. The set fails if text-only runs reach the same accuracy as runs with the trace.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Large Narration-Derived Question Set for Egocentric Video
PROPOSAL: Convert the narration sentences of public egocentric datasets into multiple-choice questions about objects, actions and episodic recall, by prompting a text model to write the question and distractor options from each narration. Sample 20000 questions across kitchens, workshops and outdoor scenes. Evaluate open multimodal models on the full set, and compare accuracy by scene type and question template.
CONTROLS: Check agreement between annotators on a subsample. Check that distractors cannot be answered by a text-only run. Check the per-template balance of answers. Report accuracy per question type.
COST: 850
PREDICTION: Models should score above chance on most templates, with episodic recall hardest. The set fails if text-only runs reach the same accuracy as video runs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fixation-Centred Visual Tokens Beside Global Tokens
PROPOSAL: Add to Qwen2.5-VL-7B a second set of visual tokens that encodes a high-detail crop centred on the fixation of each frame, appended after the global tokens with a learned marker embedding. Train only the projector on 15000 gaze-linked questions drawn from public egocentric recordings, then test on held-out wearers. Measure accuracy on attention questions and on next-action questions.
CONTROLS: Compare against the unmodified model with global tokens only on the same held-out questions. Compare against the same crop taken at a displaced point. Compare against a ring drawn on the global frames. Repeat over 3 seeds of projector initialization.
COST: 340
PREDICTION: Crops should help most when the attended object is small in the global frame. The idea fails if the displaced crop scores close to the centred crop.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Richer Global Visual Tokens for Egocentric Questions
PROPOSAL: Raise the number of global visual tokens that Qwen2.5-VL-7B builds for each frame by doubling the input image size, and feed a longer frame sequence ahead of the language model. Train only the projector on 15000 questions drawn from public egocentric recordings, then test on held-out wearers. Measure accuracy on attention questions and on next-action questions.
CONTROLS: Compare against the unmodified model with default token counts on the same held-out questions. Compare against the same model at half the frame count. Compare against a smaller image size from the same clips. Repeat over 3 seeds of projector initialization.
COST: 340
PREDICTION: Extra tokens should help most when the scene is cluttered in the global frame. The idea fails if the half-frame model scores close to the doubled model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gaze-to-Language Alignment Stage for Multimodal Models
PROPOSAL: Add a pre-training stage that teaches the projector to match crops around recorded fixations to the narration phrase spoken at that moment, using a contrastive loss over 200000 egocentric clip segments. Then instruction-tune on gaze-linked questions and evaluate on unseen wearers with fixation rings drawn on frames. Score accuracy on attention and next-action questions.
CONTROLS: Compare against instruction tuning alone from the same starting model. Compare against an alignment stage that uses crops from other segments. Compare against a ring-free evaluation of the full pipeline. Repeat over 3 seeds of projector initialization.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The alignment stage should lift accuracy on attention questions beyond instruction tuning alone. The idea fails if alignment with mismatched crops reaches the same score.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gaze Trajectory Captioning for Egocentric Video
PROPOSAL: Train a caption model that turns each fixation trajectory into a sentence describing where the wearer looked, using paired trajectories and narration text from 200000 egocentric clip segments. Score the captions against reference narrations with CIDEr and BLEU, then rank caption styles. Feed the best captions to a multimodal model in the prompt as a final check.
CONTROLS: Compare against a caption model trained on text alone from the same starting model. Compare against captions generated from trajectories of other segments. Compare against a caption-free evaluation of the full pipeline. Repeat over 3 seeds of caption model initialization.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The captions should reach higher scores on fixation-heavy segments than on static segments. The idea fails if captions from mismatched trajectories reach the same score.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Tracker Error Sensitivity of Gaze-Aided Question Answering
PROPOSAL: Compare accuracy of open multimodal models on 900 intent questions when the fixation marker comes from a research-grade tracker, from a consumer head-mounted tracker with measured calibration error, and from synthetic offsets of 1, 2, 4 and 8 degrees. Draw the marker as a ring in each case and use one fixed instruction. Plot accuracy against angular error and identify the error at which the benefit vanishes.
CONTROLS: Compare each error level against the undisturbed fixation on the same questions. Compare against a marker placed at the frame centre. Compare against frames without a marker. Repeat over 3 seeds of the offset direction.
COST: 260
PREDICTION: Accuracy should fall as angular error grows and reach the marker-free level near the object size. The idea fails if accuracy is unchanged up to the largest error.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Angular Error of Gaze Estimators on Eye Images
PROPOSAL: Evaluate 5 appearance-based gaze estimators on eye-image datasets, measuring angular error in degrees across head poses, lighting conditions and image qualities. Train each on one dataset and test on another to measure cross-dataset error, with poses binned at 10, 20, 30 and 40 degrees. Plot error against head-pose angle and identify the pose at which error rises sharply.
CONTROLS: Compare each estimator against the others on the same eye images. Compare against a predictor that always outputs the dataset mean gaze. Compare against estimators run on blurred eye images. Repeat over 3 seeds of the training split.
COST: 260
PREDICTION: Error should rise as head pose grows and reach the mean-gaze level near profile views. The idea fails if error is unchanged up to the largest pose.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Counterfactual Gaze Swap on Egocentric Intent Questions
PROPOSAL: Take 700 clips with two annotated attention targets and ask the same intent question twice, drawing the fixation of one target each time while keeping the frames identical. Measure how often open multimodal models change their answer in the direction of the marked target, and compare with swaps between unrelated clips. Break results down by question type.
CONTROLS: Compare answers under the true marker against answers under the swapped marker on the same frames. Compare against answers from a text-only run. Compare against answers with the marker removed. Repeat over 3 seeds of option order.
COST: 130
PREDICTION: Models that use the marker should switch answers when the marker moves. The idea fails if switching rates are close to those of unrelated swaps.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Vision Encoder Attention Overlap With Human Fixations
PROPOSAL: Take 700 clips and extract attention maps from the final layers of the vision encoder of open multimodal models on each frame. Measure the overlap between the encoder maps and the recorded fixation heat maps with normalised scanpath saliency, and compare with maps from unrelated clips. Break results down by question type.
CONTROLS: Compare overlap for the true fixation against overlap with a fixation from another clip. Compare against overlap with a centre-biased map. Compare against overlap from an untrained encoder. Repeat over 3 seeds of the clip subsample.
COST: 130
PREDICTION: Overlap should be higher for the true fixation than for a centre-biased map. The idea fails if overlap rates are close to those of unrelated clips.
